how_to_obtain.command: curl -sk -H 'Authorization: Bearer $IDS_API_TOKEN' https://<ids-manager>/api/v1/threat-intelligence/feeds | jq '[.[] | {name: .name, type: .feed_type, status: .status, mode: .enforcement_mode, last_sync: .last_successful_sync}] | {total_feeds: length, active_feeds: [.[] | select(.status == "active")]}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response showing active feed entries with enforcement_mode set to 'detect' or 'block' and last_sync within the last 24 hours

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the IDS threat intelligence configuration file for enabled feed connector entries and verify feed URLs, API keys, and enforcement mode settings are populated and active.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entries showing enabled=true, mode=detect or block, and populated feed URL/API credentials for at least two feed types

how_to_obtain.instruction: Trigger a test connection to a known threat intelligence feed endpoint from the IDS management host to confirm active connectivity, then verify a known malicious test indicator generates an alert.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 200 response from feed provider confirming active connectivity; recent alert log entries with 'ti.hit' or 'reputation' indicators confirming feeds are triggering detections

option_description: Controls how frequently the IDS/NIDS pulls updated threat intelligence from upstream feed providers, measured in hours. This determines the maximum age of IOC data (IP reputation lists, domain blacklists, malware hashes) used to enrich detection decisions against live network traffic.
security_impact: The Rego policy enforces that feed_refresh_interval_hours must be <= 24 for the threat_intelligence_feed_integration countermeasure to be satisfied. A stale feed means the IDS is matching traffic against outdated IOC data, allowing newly emerged malicious infrastructure (C2 IPs, phishing domains, fresh malware hashes) to pass uninspected. Feeds exceeding 24 hours are operationally stale in most threat environments where adversary infrastructure turns over within hours. Interval values of 0 or null indicate feed automation is not configured at all.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the NIDS daemon configuration directly (Suricata example) to extract the current feed update interval from the threat intelligence provider block.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output should show a numeric interval value such as 'update-interval: 3600' (seconds) or equivalent hours-based setting. Convert seconds to hours if necessary (3600s = 1h, 86400s = 24h).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the threat intelligence platform (TIP) or SIEM feed connector configuration file for the polling schedule. Applies to Zeek/Bro with intel framework, Snort with PulledPork, or standalone TIP connectors.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/pulledpork/pulledpork.conf | grep -E '(rule_url|update|cron)' && crontab -l -u snort 2>/dev/null || crontab -l -u suricata 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A cron expression (e.g., '0 */6 * * *' for every 6 hours) or explicit update_interval directive. No cron entry indicates manual or disabled refresh.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Navigate to the threat feed management panel in the SIEM or dedicated TIP console (e.g., MISP, OpenCTI, ThreatConnect, or vendor NIDS GUI) to review feed synchronization schedules.
how_to_obtain.navigation: SIEM Console > Threat Intelligence > Feed Management > [Select Feed] > Sync Schedule / Polling Interval. For Cisco Secure IDS: Configuration > Threat Intelligence > Feed Sources > Edit > Update Frequency. For Palo Alto Panorama: Objects > External Dynamic Lists > [List] > Repeat.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A numeric interval displayed in hours or minutes alongside a 'Last Synced' timestamp. Compare last sync time to current time to verify the configured interval is actually executing.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the SIEM or TIP REST API to retrieve feed source configurations programmatically, including polling interval and last successful pull metadata.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response listing each feed with its refresh interval in seconds/hours and last_successful_sync ISO timestamp. Divide seconds by 3600 to normalize to hours.

typical_values: 6 (every 6 hours — common for commercial TIP integrations)
168 (weekly — common in under-resourced or misconfigured environments, fails policy)

option_description: Defines the set of IOC category types actively ingested from threat intelligence feeds and applied to network traffic inspection. Each element represents a distinct IOC class such as 'ip_reputation', 'domain_blacklist', 'malware_hash', or 'url_blacklist'. Only feed types listed here are parsed, matched, and acted upon by the IDS detection engine.
security_impact: The Rego policy requires count(input.active_feed_types) >= 2 for basic countermeasure satisfaction, and specifically checks for both 'ip_reputation' and 'domain_blacklist' as a named passing condition. An empty array (the default) means zero threat intelligence enrichment is applied to network decisions — the IDS operates purely on signatures and behavioral rules with no IOC context. Restricting to a single feed type creates blind spots: an ip_reputation-only configuration will miss domain-fronted C2 traffic; a malware_hash-only configuration provides no network-layer blocking. Breadth of active feed types directly correlates to detection coverage against known-bad infrastructure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate active intel feed source types configured in the IDS engine (Suricata with suricata-update or Zeek Intel Framework) to list which IOC categories are currently loaded and matched.
how_to_obtain.command: suricata-update list-enabled-sources 2>/dev/null && ls -la /var/lib/suricata/rules/ | grep -iE '(reputation|blacklist|hash|ioc|intel)' && zeek -e 'print Intel::read_files' 2>/dev/null || cat /opt/zeek/share/zeek/site/intel/*.dat 2>/dev/null | head -5
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of rule/feed files loaded into the engine. Files named 'ip-reputation.rules', 'domain-blacklist.conf', 'malware-hashes.ioc' indicate active feed types. No such files indicate the array is effectively empty.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the IDS/TIP integration configuration to identify which IOC category subscriptions are enabled and parsed. Check both the feed source configuration and the indicator type filter settings.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration entries listing enabled IOC types per feed source. Example: 'indicator_types: [ip_reputation, domain_blacklist]'. An absence of indicator_type filters may indicate all types are accepted or none are explicitly configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the active feed subscriptions and IOC type filters in the threat intelligence management interface of the SIEM, TIP, or NIDS console to confirm which categories are being ingested and matched.
how_to_obtain.navigation: For MISP: Administration > Server Settings > MISP > Connected Servers > [Feed] > Enabled Event Types. For Cisco Secure IDS: Configuration > Threat Intelligence > Active Indicators > Filter by Type. For Splunk ES: Configure > Data Enrichment > Threat Intelligence Sources > [Source] > Indicator Types. For Palo Alto: Objects > External Dynamic Lists > Type column (IP List, URL List, Domain List).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A checklist or tag list showing which IOC types are toggled active. Confirm at minimum 'ip_reputation' and 'domain_blacklist' are enabled and showing a non-zero indicator count.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect IDS alert logs and feed ingestion logs to identify which IOC type categories are generating matches, providing empirical evidence of which feed types are actually active and producing detections.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -E '(ET Intelligence|reputation|blacklist|hash_match|ioc_match|feed_hit)' /var/log/suricata/fast.log /var/log/suricata/eve.json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.alert.category' 2>/dev/null | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Alert categories referencing IOC feed types (e.g., 'Misc Attack - IP Reputation', 'DNS Blacklist Hit', 'Malware Hash Match'). Zero results for a given category over a 24-hour window suggests that feed type is not active, misconfigured, or producing no traffic matches.

typical_values: [] (empty default — zero TI enrichment, fails all Rego conditions)
